summary: System design question bank that uses all ten portfolio projects (rate limiter, mini-Redis, job queue, webhooks, mini-Kafka, multi-tenant SaaS, object storage, collaborative editing, payments, workflow engine) as concrete evidence. Each answer is a structured design walkthrough -- clarify requirements, estimate scale, API, data model, core flow, failure handling, scaling to 10x/100x, trade-offs -- and cites real files, real bugs and measured numbers from the projects' TESTING.md files. Covers classic designs (payments, Kafka, S3, Google Docs, Redis cluster, webhook platform, rate limiter, workflow engine, multi-tenant SaaS) and cross-cutting themes (idempotency, exactly-once myths, outbox, sagas vs workflows, leases and fencing, queue choice, backpressure, multi-region, observability, consistency models, bottleneck hunting).

pitch.intro_30s: Maine backend aur distributed systems ke core problems ko samajhne ke liye das chhote par production-style systems banaye hain: rate limiter, Redis-like DB, job queue, webhook platform, Kafka-like log, multi-tenant SaaS, S3-like storage, Google-Docs-style collab, payments aur Temporal-style workflow engine. System design round mein main inhe evidence ki tarah use karta hoon: 'yeh design maine banaya, yeh bug aaya, yeh number measure kiya, isliye yeh trade-off'.
pitch.explain_2min:
Main system design questions ko ek fixed structure se answer karta hoon -- requirements clarify, scale estimate, API, data model, core flow, failures, 10x/100x scaling, trade-offs -- aur har step pe apne projects se concrete evidence deta hoon.

Das projects ek dusre se jude hue hain. Correctness ke building blocks har jagah repeat hote hain: idempotency keys (payments, webhooks, job queue, Kafka producer, workflow activities), leases plus fencing tokens (job queue mein attempt number, webhooks mein attempts column, workflow engine mein heartbeats), aur transactional outbox (webhooks mein event plus delivery rows ek transaction mein). Storage side pe maine Redis jaisa single-threaded store, Kafka jaisa segmented replicated log, aur S3 jaisa metadata/data split banaya. Coordination ke liye Postgres SKIP LOCKED queues, Redis Lua scripts, row-lock sequencer (collab) aur deterministic replay (workflow engine).

Interview mein sabse valuable cheez yeh hai ki har project ke TESTING.md mein real numbers aur real bugs hain. Jaise webhooks mein maine phase timing se pata kiya ki 116ms DB record mein ja rahe the aur HTTP send sirf 1.7ms -- fix ke baad 48 se 111 deliveries/s. Kafka clone mein cProfile ne dikhaya ki Windows pe just-written file open karna 65% time le raha tha -- reusable handle se 7.7x. SaaS mein ek RLS policy ka OR clause cross-tenant privilege escalation de raha tha, test ne pakda. Payments mein timeout ko 'unknown' maana, failure nahi.

Isliye jab interviewer 'design a payment system' ya 'design Kafka' poochta hai, main textbook answer ke saath bata sakta hoon ki kaunsa part maine actually implement kiya, kaunsa honestly nahi (multi-region, Redis Cluster), aur production mein next step kya hota.
pitch.deep_5min:
Main ek concrete flow se shuru karta hoon jo kai projects ko chhuta hai: customer checkout karta hai.

Request pehle edge pe aati hai. Wahan authentication -- SaaS project mein JWT ya hashed API key se Principal banta hai jisme tenant, role aur plan hota hai -- aur rate limiting. Rate limiter project mein maine paanch algorithms Redis Lua scripts mein likhe, kyunki local counters 3 instances pe 3x overshoot karte hain (test se proven: limit 50, in-memory 150 allow). Redis ka TIME use hota hai taaki app servers ka clock skew matter na kare. Har policy ka fail mode alag: normal APIs fail-open, login fail-closed. Load testing mein do real bugs mile: connection pool exhaust hone ko code ne 'Redis down' samjha aur silently fail-open kar diya, aur synchronous logging ne event loop block karke false timeouts banaye.

Phir payment. Payments project mein Idempotency-Key ka row pehle insert hota hai with request hash; same key different body pe 422, in progress pe 409. State machine compare-and-set se chalti hai, provider call hamesha DB transaction ke bahar, aur provider ko same idempotency key ke saath retry. Timeout aaye toh payment 'requires_reconciliation' mein jaata hai -- kyunki timeout ka matlab pata nahi hota ki charge hua ya nahi. Recovery worker provider se lookup karke resolve karta hai. Ledger double-entry hai aur balance invariant ek deferred constraint trigger enforce karta hai, toh app bug paisa create nahi kar sakta. Measured: ek authorize+capture 26 SQL statements, sequential 7.5 payments/s on my Docker Desktop setup -- slow, par har crash point recoverable, aur yeh trade maine deliberately liya.

Checkout ke multiple steps -- inventory, charge, ship -- payments project mein saga with compensations hai. Uski limitation honest hai: process crash mid-saga ke baad auto-resume nahi. Wahi problem workflow engine project solve karta hai: workflow code ka har step event history mein, workers stateless, koi bhi worker replay karke resume kare. Non-deterministic deploy pe workflow fail nahi hota, blocked rehta hai, rollback pe resume. Cost: replay history ke saath super-linear -- 2,001 events ka replay 102-132 ms measured -- isliye production engines sticky cache aur continue-as-new rakhte hain.

Payment ke baad side effects: email aur merchant ko webhook. Email job queue project se jaata hai: Redis sorted sets, har state transition ek Lua script, attempt number fencing token. Worker ko kill -9 kiya test mein, dusre process ne job dobara chalaya, aur processed_jobs ledger same transaction mein hone ki wajah se exactly ek email row bani. Webhook platform mein event aur har subscriber ki delivery row ek transaction mein -- outbox aur queue same rows. Dispatchers SKIP LOCKED se claim karte hain, SSRF check send time pe hota hai aur connection validated IP pe pinned hai (DNS rebinding fix), signatures Standard Webhooks format mein, rotation dual-signature se.

Agar volume bahut badhe toh events Kafka-style log mein jaate hain. Mere minikafka mein segmented log, ISR, high watermark, acks, consumer groups with generation fencing, aur idempotent producer hai. acks=1 pe failover data loss ek test prove karta hai. Batching sabse bada lever nikla: HTTP producer batch 1 pe 376 msg/s, batch 1000 pe 32,841.

Aur supporting systems: invoices/attachments S3-like storage mein (bytes first, metadata second, orphans GC), collaborative notes Google-Docs-style OT ke saath jahan Postgres row lock sequencer hai aur Redis pub/sub fan-out with gap fill, aur poora product multi-tenant SaaS pe jahan Postgres RLS backstop hai.

Hardest decisions jo main interview mein highlight karta hoon: timeout ko unknown maanna; Postgres queue vs Redis queue (atomicity vs speed); fencing tokens ka storage-side check; aur 'exactly-once delivery' ko reject karke 'at-least-once plus idempotent effects' bolna. Aur main honestly batata hoon kya nahi banaya: multi-region, Redis Cluster mode, real network partitions in the Kafka clone, real payment provider.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough:
Main portfolio ko layers mein explain karta hoon.

Edge aur access: Project 1 (rate limiter: Redis Lua algorithms, policies, fail modes, Prometheus metrics) aur Project 6 (multi-tenant SaaS: JWT + refresh rotation, hashed scoped API keys, RBAC + ABAC, plans/quotas, Postgres RLS, audit log). Project 7 ka HMAC request signing aur presigned URLs, aur Project 8 ke one-time WebSocket tickets bhi isi layer ke patterns hain.

State aur storage engines: Project 2 (single-threaded RESP server, expiry, eviction, AOF/snapshots, async replication), Project 5 (segmented commit log, sparse index, ISR, high watermark, controller elections, consumer groups), Project 7 (object storage: Postgres metadata + pluggable blob adapter, versioning, multipart, lifecycle, GC).

Async processing aur delivery: Project 3 (Redis job queue with leases, fencing, backoff, DLQ, schedules, idempotent handlers), Project 4 (Postgres outbox + SKIP LOCKED dispatchers, signing, SSRF, rate limits, auto-disable, replay).

Business correctness: Project 9 (payments: idempotency keys, state machine, double-entry ledger enforced in DB, recovery worker, reconciliation, saga) aur Project 10 (durable workflow engine: event history, deterministic replay, activities with retries/heartbeats, timers, signals, cancellation).

Real-time: Project 8 (OT, central sequencer, WebSockets, Redis pub/sub with ordered forwarder and gap fill, offline sync, history/snapshots).

Shared: `shared/bpcommon` (JSON logging via QueueHandler, errors). Har project ke saath README, ARCHITECTURE, TRADEOFFS, FAILURE_SCENARIOS, SECURITY aur TESTING docs hain; TESTING.md mein measured numbers aur fixed bugs.
difficult_decisions: Payments mein provider timeout ko failure nahi, 'requires_reconciliation' maanna -- recovery worker aur extra state ki complexity li, taaki double charge ya 'charged but no order' kabhi na ho.
Webhooks mein Postgres ko outbox aur queue dono banana (SKIP LOCKED) instead of Redis/Kafka -- publish ek ACID transaction, par per-delivery DB cost; measured ceiling ke baad Kafka relay ka plan.

Job queue mein Redis for mechanics, Postgres for effects -- atomic fast state transitions, aur idempotency record + side effect same transaction mein; cost: enqueue producer ki DB transaction ke saath atomic nahi.
Collab mein Postgres row lock ko sequencer banana -- koi bhi server koi bhi edit le sakta hai aur failover trivial, par per-document throughput ~45-66 ops/s pe bounded.
Workflow engine mein non-deterministic deploy pe workflow fail karne ke bajaye blocked rakhna -- rollback se recovery, par error field ki monitoring zaroori.
Rate limiter mein per-policy fail mode: availability ke liye fail-open, login ke liye fail-closed -- aur auth hamesha fail-closed with 503.
biggest_challenges: Multi-tenant SaaS mein RLS policy ke 'OR user_id = app.user_id' ne cross-tenant privilege escalation diya: non-member ko tenant A ka owner role mil gaya. HTTP isolation test ne pakda (expected 404, got 200); strict policy + SECURITY DEFINER function + regression test se fix.

Webhook throughput 48 deliveries/s pe atka tha. Phase timing ne dikhaya `_record` 116ms vs HTTP send 1.7ms; WAL fsync hypothesis synchronous_commit=off se reject hui. Claim mein saara data CTE se aur record ek statement mein -> 111/s (1 dispatcher), 189/s (3).

Kafka clone mein acks=all 8,702 msg/s pe slow tha. Timer resolution aur slow reads dono hypotheses reject; cProfile ne `io.open` 65% time dikhaya (Windows pe just-written file open slow). Reusable read handle -> 73,795 msg/s (7.7x).

Rate limiter load test mein synchronous logging ne event loop block kiya, 50ms Redis timeouts false fire hue, 67 HTTP 500s aur 357 allowed instead of 300. QueueHandler logging + 250ms timeout + BlockingConnectionPool se fix.

Job queue ke lease keeper mein error handling nahi thi: ek transient Redis error ke baad lease extension band -> silent expiry -> duplicate execution. Regression test ke saath fix; fencing ne results ko safe rakha tha, par effect ke liye idempotency hi bachav thi.
failure_scenarios: Worker kill -9 mid-job (job queue, workflow engine): lease expire, dusra worker attempt 2 chalata hai, fencing purane worker ka ack reject karta hai, idempotent handler duplicate effect rokta hai.
Provider timeout during capture (payments): requires_reconciliation, recovery same key se retry ya lookup karke resolve; ledger exactly once book hota hai.
Kafka leader crash: acks=all ke saath committed data safe, acks=1 pe acknowledged write lose (test se proven); last ISR member wapas aaye toh partition recover (review fix).
Redis outage: rate limiter fail-open/closed per policy, job queue stalls (source of truth), SaaS limits fail-open, collab fan-out ruk jaata hai par commits Postgres mein safe, gap fill se recovery.
Crash between blob write and metadata commit (object storage): orphan blob, GC grace period ke baad delete; dangling metadata kabhi nahi.
Bad workflow deploy: NonDeterminismError record, workflow blocked, rollback pe resume -- koi data fix nahi chahiye.
improvements: Multi-region design implement nahi hai: next step home-region-per-tenant routing, async replicas, aur epoch-based fencing for failover.
Webhooks aur workflow engine ke Postgres queues ke upar outbox relay into a partitioned log (minikafka/Kafka) jab thousands/s ka ceiling aaye; delivery_attempts aur history ko time partitions.
Redis Cluster readiness: rate limiter aur job queue ke Lua scripts mein dynamically built keys ko KEYS mein declare karna aur hash tags per queue.
End-to-end tracing (OpenTelemetry) with trace ids job payloads, outbox rows aur workflow history mein; abhi structured logs, metrics aur audit tables hain.
Kafka clone mein leader-epoch truncation (KIP-101) aur replicated idempotent producer state; workflow engine mein versioning API aur sticky cache.
Secrets (webhook signing, access keys) ko KMS envelope encryption ke saath store karna; abhi plaintext documented limitation hai.

steps: 1. Concept: har design answer ka skeleton -- clarify requirements, estimate scale, API, data model, core flow, failure handling, 10x/100x scaling, trade-offs.
2. Why here: das projects ka evidence tabhi kaam aata hai jab answer structured ho; warna details mein kho jaate ho.
3. API/code: payments project ka API_DOCUMENTATION aur ARCHITECTURE padho -- API, state machine, sequence diagram ek saath.
4. Implementation detail: dekho ki capture flow mein intent -> provider call -> result kaise alag transactions hain (services/payments.py).
5. Demonstrate: 'Design a payment system' khud 5 minute mein bolo using SYSD-001 skeleton; timer lagao.
6. Interviewer next: 'what happens if the provider times out?' -- requires_reconciliation aur recovery worker se answer karo.
1. Concept: retry safe tabhi jab operation idempotent ho; stable key har hop pe.
2. Why here: payments, webhooks, job queue, Kafka producer aur workflow activities sab retries pe depend karte hain.
3. API/code: payments `idempotency.py::begin` (request hash, in_progress lease, stored response).
4. Implementation detail: webhooks `events.py::publish` mein ON CONFLICT race loser winner return karta hai; job queue mein processed_jobs same tx.
5. Demonstrate: job queue `tests/test_crash_process.py` chalao -- real worker process kill, exactly 1 email row.
6. Interviewer next: 'two concurrent requests with the same key?' aur 'how long do you keep keys?'
1. Concept: lease = time-bound ownership; fencing token = monotonic number jo storage check karta hai.
2. Why here: workers crash ya pause hote hain; bina fencing ke zombie writes results overwrite karte hain.
3. API/code: job queue `claim.lua` attempts++ aur `ack.lua` token check.
4. Implementation detail: webhooks `RECORD_SQL` WHERE attempts = :attempt; workflow engine heartbeats with attempt.
5. Demonstrate: job queue `test_visibility_timeout_reaper_and_fencing` aur webhooks `test_crashed_dispatcher_lease_expires_and_zombie_result_is_rejected`.
6. Interviewer next: 'why is Redlock unsafe without fencing?' aur 'how do you fence an external HTTP call?' (you can't -- idempotency key).
1. Concept: dual write avoid karne ke liye event ko business change ke saath ek transaction mein likho.
2. Why here: webhooks outbox = queue; job queue ka Redis enqueue isse lacking hai (TRADEOFFS #1).
3. API/code: webhooks `publish` (event + deliveries one tx) aur `CLAIM_SQL` (SKIP LOCKED + lease).
4. Implementation detail: Redis (Lua, fast) vs Postgres (atomic with data) vs Kafka (replay, throughput) compare karo using each TRADEOFFS.md.
5. Demonstrate: webhooks `test_publish_is_atomic` aur `test_three_dispatchers_deliver_each_exactly_once`.
6. Interviewer next: 'polling relay vs CDC?' aur 'when does the Postgres queue stop scaling?'
1. Concept: durability = local fsync policy + replication policy; RPO isi se nikalta hai.
2. Why here: mini-Redis async replication aur minikafka acks/ISR dono failover loss ko demonstrate karte hain.
3. API/code: minikafka `cluster.py` (`_check_isr`, `_elect`), mini-Redis `persistence/aof.py`.
4. Implementation detail: high watermark = min LEO of ISR; consumers sirf HW ke neeche padhte hain; AOF group commit.
5. Demonstrate: `test_acks_1_can_lose_acknowledged_write_on_failover` aur `test_leader_failover_keeps_committed_data`.
6. Interviewer next: 'what is KIP-101?' aur 'how do you avoid split brain?'
1. Concept: multi-step process bina 2PC -- local commits + compensations; workflow engine use durable banata hai.
2. Why here: payments saga crash-resume nahi karta; workflow engine replay se karta hai.
3. API/code: payments `saga.py::checkout`/`compensate`; workflow engine `runtime.py::replay`, `store.py::complete_workflow_task`.
4. Implementation detail: determinism rules (ctx.now), optimistic commit on last_event_id, activity idempotency keys.
5. Demonstrate: `test_worker_crash_another_worker_resumes_from_history` aur `test_nondeterministic_deploy_is_detected_and_workflow_survives`.
6. Interviewer next: 'how do you version workflow code?' aur 'what if a compensation fails?'
1. Concept: defence in depth -- authn -> Principal -> authz -> DB-level RLS -> audit.
2. Why here: SaaS ka OR-policy escalation bug dikhata hai ki app checks akela kaafi nahi.
3. API/code: SaaS `db/session.py::tenant_tx` (SET LOCAL), `core/rbac.py`; object storage `services/signing.py`.
4. Implementation detail: migration 0003 strict policy; API key perms = scopes AND creator's current role.
5. Demonstrate: SaaS `tests/test_rls.py` aur `bench/rls_bench.py` (0.148 ms with index vs 2.938 ms without).
6. Interviewer next: 'when would you move a tenant to its own DB?' aur 'how do you prevent tenant enumeration?'
1. Concept: honest harness -> measure -> hypothesis -> one change -> confirm/reject -> re-measure.
2. Why here: har project ke TESTING.md mein rejected hypotheses aur real fixes documented hain.
3. API/code: webhooks `bench/phase_timing.py` aur `bench/bench_drain.py`; minikafka `bench/bench.py`.
4. Implementation detail: client vs server time alag karo, CPU% of wall check karo (CPU-bound detection), EXPLAIN ANALYZE for SQL.
5. Demonstrate: webhooks TESTING.md ka story bolo -- 7,526/s fake number, 116ms record, synchronous_commit=off rejected, 48 -> 111/s.
6. Interviewer next: 'p99 doubled in production, what do you check first?'
